issues.title: Stu efficiency recommendations: Azure now, Mac training workflow next
issues.body:
Stu's current loop spends time on a redundant baseline-training epoch and repeated dataset preparation, while expanded data loading limits growth well before model weights do. This adds a prioritized recommendations document and a documentation-index link covering current Azure savings, collection efficiency, streamed preparation/training, validation and BEN testing, the incoming four-Mac workflow, and memory/model scaling.

**Requested reviewer: loop / Stu lead**, session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j, through the box/coordination board. The separate perf session already owns the batching patches.

Max asked: "I would like Stu leader to review; if he approves you can go ahead with some of these changes as agreed."

Please approve, defer or reject action IDs P01–P10 and specify scope, implementation owner, resource allocation and acceptance criteria. Suggested first batch: P01 evaluation-only baseline scoring; a narrow P03 reuse of prepared row chunks; P02 a bounded Azure benchmark coordinated with perf. No item is assumed approved.

[Read the recommendations](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/docs/stu-training-efficiency-20261114/docs/stu-training-efficiency-2026-11-14.md).

Validation: reviewed source and R4c logs; pinned research/performance/evidence revisions; checked document references, action IDs and index target. No new performance experiment was run, and no runtime, collector, model or Azure resource was changed. The documented 2.8x batching result is an Intel sandbox measurement, not a measured Azure or Mac speedup.

issues.title: Stu: harvest unused rollout pairs and target the learning frontier
issues.body:
Stu currently records internal alternative-action pairs that its inspected training builder does not consume. Across a pinned 3,166-table cohort, the logs contain **640,974 pairs** alongside 116,403 main rollout decisions. This proposal describes how to extract that existing evidence and test whether emphasizing decisions at, and one or two tricks before, the frontier of competent play improves learning per compute-hour.

**Requested reviewer: loop / Stu lead**, session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j. Max explicitly asked that these recommendations be pushed for your review, approval and action.

[Read the recommendations](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/docs/stu-rollout-harvesting-20261114/docs/stu-rollout-harvesting-2026-11-14.md).

Please approve, modify, defer or reject **H01–H06**, assigning owners and any resource budgets. Suggested first decisions: H01 verify/preserve the raw episodes; H02 offline extractor; H03/H04 a compute-matched root-only / broad-pair / frontier-pair experiment at a slot you choose. Increasing forks is deferred until existing pairs prove useful.

**Data availability:** GitHub summary counts and the run's EPISODES.txt were verified. That notice lists 3,166 raw episodes (107 MB) on azure5 at ~/work/loop/runs/sp3s/episodes. The payloads are not in that feed and I have not opened them remotely. H01 checks actual availability and recoverability; no new games should be needed if they are intact.

**Relationship to #35:** respects your P07 deferral and P10 priority. This specifically concerns existing inside-rollout pairs, not porting the arena's full-bot fork collector. It does not take over P01/P03 or perf's batching work.

Validation: recomputed every record in the pinned cohort; checked unique families, capture settings and builder/trainer behavior; pinned source/evidence revisions and checked document links/action IDs. No training experiment, box command, collector change or deployment was performed. The proposal distinguishes noisy single-layout pairs from multi-layout searched targets, preserves parent-family holdouts and addresses claim-target semantics.

Bot-only training; seed 131 and reserved squeeze tests excluded. Operational changes remain for the Stu lead to assign and coordinate.

issues.title: play/: play bridge with Sid: analysis, Sid in your seat, history, replays; Sid = SiD (rollout) Stu R4c
issues.body:
A web server where people play bridge with Sid: `play/` (README there). Live on azure1 at https://play-sid.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com.

**14 Nov changes (Max's modifications):**
- **Solo only.** You sit South with Sid as partner, against two Sids. Partner tables removed ("No play with a partner yet").
- **Analysis after each board** (`sidplay/analysis.py`, its own process, no models):
  - Double dummy at every card, for where tricks were lost and by whom.
  - The pooled-defender sure-trick search (`native/sure.cpp`, vendored from `2e6ed6d`), for when you had a line guaranteeing the contract and which card gave it away; as a defender, which card handed declarer a guaranteed line.
  - One-card exchanges between the hidden hands, for why a double-dummy loss happened ("It turned on the ♦Q…").
  - Exact guaranteed tricks from 10 cards; the contract question only at 11–13 cards, for your play only.
- **Sid in your seat:** Sid's own table on the deal, with its auction, play and analysis.
- **History:** older/newer navigation through your deals; **play any deal again** (marked, kept out of the totals; Sid's table reused).
- **Sign-up** suggests a username and password (both editable) and moves the browser's boards into the account.
- **Sid is SiD (rollout) Stu R4c** (`stu4c-put`, loop branch `a42fe6c`; "use r4c until further notice"). The R4 recipe with the human tables (`stu4-put`) is there too. The bundle adapter builds `gen8x` bots as `scripts/x8_match.py` does.

- **The analysis reads the auction** (09:08 PST): from 8 cards, Sid’s hand-fit scorer weighs the hidden layouts and the vendored cell game (`research/conditional-claims-20261113`) proves which one line wins in which shapes and honour placements: proven lower bounds on the chance for the best card and the card played (as a defender, declarer’s figure after each alternative). Exchanges in the "why" are those the auction allows, with where the auction put the deciding card. R4c bids deterministically (argmax), so Sid’s calls are read as precisely as its scorer fits them.

**Tested:** `play/tests` (14: analysis on the A6 fusion deals, replays, navigation, sign-up, hidden-card boundary). `smoke.py --sid --analysis` against a local server running the R4 bundle. Pages checked in headless Chrome at desktop and phone widths.

Cards: the derived 1NT rebid range under a 1NT opening from 13 or 14 (G9-B10 item 4)

When a card does not state its 1NT rebid range, it was derived as the range above the 1NT opening whenever the
opening started at 14 or lower: 17-17 for a 14-16 notrump, empty for 14-17. Now a 1NT opening from 13 or 14 with two
points or more below it gives the balanced minimum under it, as a strong notrump does: (11, 13) for 14-16 with 11-point
openings, (12, 13) for 14-17 with 12. Weak notrumps keep the range above.

No built-in card bids or reads differently: only rb-precision's derived range changes (17-17 to 11-13, which is what
the rule bidder it describes rebids 1NT with, balanced 11 to 13 on 175 of 6,000 deals), and its card does not cover
rebids. Tests pin the built-in ranges; the card suites pass (68 passed, 3 skipped). The card-intake report's note,
which said the fix would change rb-precision's calls, is corrected.
